submission.natural_language_explanation: Retrospective negation-scope detector. Its strong, general response (about 0.5-2.7) is to the token that sits inside the scope of a negator earlier in the clause (not, n't, never, no, nobody, nothing, without, hardly, cannot): the pole peaks on the polarity-sensitive or light word the negation licenses (any, ever, anything, anyone, at all, all, way, just) and on the light word that continues the negated predicate (to, the, a, like, want, some), and it falls to the floor (<=0.15) when that negator is replaced by an affirmative word (also, often, one, all, with) or when the peak token is replaced by a non-polarity synonym. In affirmative text the pole only reaches a weaker 0.15-0.5 band, on degree/quantifier modifiers (much, more, far, very, too, even, both, lower) and on scattered single content words that complete a familiar phrase (central, rain, increased, captured, of), so text with no negator and none of those tokens is predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The defendant also pleaded guilty to all charges.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Example 1 with the negator replaced by the affirmative word 'also'; the hypothesis explicitly predicts the floor even though the peak token 'all' is retained.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The senator announced she would also seek re-election next year.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Example 3 with 'not' replaced by 'also'; the hypothesis predicts the floor on 'seek'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Do you have any questions about the schedule?
adversarial_test_results.detail: Question licensing places 'any' before a noun with no negator in the clause, and the hypothesis predicts no activation without a negator.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: You can pick any seat in the auditorium.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Affirmative free-choice 'any' with no negator anywhere in the text; predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: This is the best pizza I have ever eaten.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Affirmative superlative 'ever' with no negator to license it; predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: I just want some water before we leave.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The light words just/want/some appear with no negated predicate to continue, so the hypothesis predicts they do not fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The notice on the board announced a staff meeting on Friday.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'notice' shares letters with 'not' but is not the negator token, so the hypothesis predicts the floor.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The exam was hard for most students in the class.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'hard' is the stem of 'hardly' but is not a negator token, and no other trigger is present; predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The technician explained the procedure. He did not. The manager signed the form on Friday.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The negator is clause-final with no following in-scope token, and the later light words sit in a separate sentence, so retrospective scope predicts no activation.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: UPDATE users SET active = 1 WHERE name LIKE 'A%';
adversarial_test_results.detail: SQL near-miss to example 6 with no negator, so the hypothesis predicts the floor on the keyword LIKE and the other tokens.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Nobody told me anything about the schedule change.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Novel negator 'nobody' scoping 'anything' (and 'the'); the hypothesis predicts a strong peak on 'anything'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He hardly ever visits his parents these days.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'hardly' licenses 'ever' in a context unlike the examples; predicted active.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She left the party without saying goodbye to anyone.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The negator 'without' scopes 'anyone' and the light word 'to'; the hypothesis predicts a strong peak here.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: I cannot just ignore the warning on the label.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Novel negator 'cannot' with the light word 'just' inside its scope; predicted active.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The quarterly review began on a cool morning in early April, when the finance team gathered in the conference room on the fourth floor. Each analyst brought a printed summary of the accounts, a laptop, and a folder of supporting documents. The chair opened the meeting by outlining the agenda: revenue recognition, inventory valuation, travel expenses, and the timetable for the annual audit. For the first hour the group walked through the income statement line by line, comparing each figure with the budget approved in January. Sales in the northern region had grown steadily through the winter, while the southern region held roughly flat. The marketing department spent slightly less than planned, mainly because two trade shows were postponed until the autumn. After a short break, the discussion moved to inventory. The warehouse manager reported that stock levels had fallen in line with expectations, although a batch of components arrived later than scheduled. She explained how the team counted every pallet at the end of March and reconciled the totals with the ledger. Several small discrepancies turned up in the records for spare parts, and the accounting staff agreed to investigate them before the next review. The chair asked whether the revised shipping contract would affect the cost of goods sold in the second quarter. The controller said the change would shift some freight charges into a later period, which should smooth the reported margin. Lunch arrived at noon, and the conversation turned to the new reporting software. A junior analyst demonstrated how the system imports data from the sales database, checks each entry against the customer master file, and flags unusual patterns for manual review. The team agreed that the tool saved several hours of routine work each week. One member raised a question about access rights, and the chair promised to follow up with the information security group. In the afternoon the group reviewed travel expenses, sampling receipts from the spring conference season. Two claims were missing a manager's signature, and the clerk was asked to request the required approval from the relevant department head. The auditors ultimately found no evidence of any misconduct in the quarterly accounts. With that item closed, the chair thanked everyone for the careful preparation and set the date for the next meeting. The team left the room in good spirits, carrying action items and a revised list of deadlines. Outside the window the city was busy with traffic, and the afternoon sun lit the glass towers along the river. A few colleagues stayed behind to finish their notes, while the rest returned to their desks to update the working papers. The review had covered a wide range of topics, from revenue and inventory to software and travel, and the mood remained calm and constructive throughout the day. Everyone agreed that the process was thorough, and the chair closed the session by wishing the group a pleasant weekend. The minutes would be circulated on Monday, and corrections could be raised at the start of the following session.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A roughly 520-token financial-audit passage with 'no evidence of any' buried deep inside; the hypothesis predicts a strong peak on 'any' in this unseen, different-genre long context.
